1.why: Every MFA endpoint (settings, setup, confirm, recovery/verify, backup/regenerate) calls owner(request), which derives the user solely from the HttpOnly server-side session and requires session.userId === ACCOUNT.id, and manipulated() rejects injected userId/accountId/ownerId/email fields.

2.why: The identity verification code is generated per pre-auth session (session.identityCode) and verified only against that session with a matching CSRF token and session.userId === ACCOUNT.id, so one session's code cannot be used by any other session or user.

3.why: The /api/mfa/confirm handler stores the MFA record but never invalidates the confirming session or any other existing sessions, and logout deletes only the current session, so pre-existing sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: TOTP secrets are stored as AES-GCM ciphertext (encryptSecret/encryptedSecret) and backup codes are stored only as HMAC-SHA-256 hashes in backupHashes; plaintext secrets/codes are never persisted.

5.why: All secrets, session tokens, CSRF tokens, identity codes, TOTP seeds, and backup codes are generated via crypto.getRandomValues, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: The client keeps the CSRF token, setup secret, and codes only in in-memory JS variables (no localStorage/sessionStorage), and the only cookie is the __Host-mfa_session cookie marked HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict.

7.why: The server validates email, phone, OTP, and backup code formats with strict regexes (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validBackup), enforces JSON content-type and a 4KB body cap, and no SQL is used so injection via queries is not applicable.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered via textContent (displayName, setup secret, codes) while innerHTML is used only with static templates, and a nonce-based CSP (script-src 'nonce-...') further blocks injected script execution.

9.why: The application contains no redirect endpoints or Location headers at all (navigation is client-side function calls), so open redirects are impossible, though no explicit redirect allow-list mechanism exists to point to.

10.why: The headers() function sets CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS (max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits __Host-mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, and a Max-Age, and the logout path sets an expired cookie with the same attributes.

12.why: Server-side errors are generic with no stack traces and nothing sensitive appears in URLs or server logs, but the client log() function deliberately writes the identity verification code, the current TOTP code, and the backup codes to the browser console and a visible Logs panel, and API responses include testCode/testOtp, so codes are in fact exposed in logs.

13.why: The identity code expires after 10 minutes and its session is destroyed on success, TOTP counters are recorded in usedCounters to prevent replay within the 30-second window, and backup codes are deleted from backupHashes after a single use.

14.why: Identity, authenticator, and recovery verification all apply throttling with MAX_FAILURES=5 leading to a 10-minute lockout (identityThrottles keyed durably on submitted details, authenticatorThrottles, and recoveryAttempts/recoveryLockedUntil), returning 429 while locked.

15.why: On successful verification the pre-auth session is deleted and a fresh authenticated session with a new random ID is issued (rotation), authenticated sessions enforce 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts (pre-auth 10 minutes), and /api/auth/logout deletes the session server-side and expires the cookie.
